question: Acquisition of the weekly magazine Challenges and the implementation of the European Media Freedom Act

The European Media Freedom Act (EMFA)1 sets out obligations regarding the assessment of media monopolies and safeguards against political or economic interference. In France, the magazine Challenges is about to be acquired by LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton.

This group already owns most of the media outlets in the economic and financial press market, which raises concerns about a monopoly and abuse of a dominant position. Furthermore, France has not yet designated the national regulatory authority responsible for assessing this type of acquisition, as provided for in Article 22 EMFA.
Considering the situation, the Commission must implement the EMFA to guarantee media pluralism and ensure editorial independence. 1.
Has France referred the matter to the Commission under Article 22 EMFA for it to assess the impact of this acquisition?

Under Article 23 EMFA, given the absence of a national evaluation, does the Commission intend to refer this acquisition to the European Board for Media Services to assess its impact on monopolies in the relevant market?

How does the Commission intend to coordinate the application of the EMFA with Regulation 139/20042 on the control of concentrations between undertakings, ensuring that competition in the internal market is not distorted?
OJ L, 2024/1083, 17.4.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1083/oj. OJ L 24, 29.1.2004, pp. 1–22, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2004/139/oj.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.2.2026) The Media Board has not, at this stage, been consulted or informed by the French authorities under Article 22 of European Media Freedom Act (EMFA)1 concerning the envisaged acquisition of the magazine ‘Challenges’. It is for Member States to enable an appropriate national assessment of media market concentrations falling within the scope of Article 22.
The Commission remains in close contact with the French authorities regarding the designation of the competent national authority foreseen by the EMFA.

In the absence of an assessment by the national regulatory authority or body concerned or a consultation of the Media Board under Article 22, the Media Board shall draw up, on its own initiative or at the request of the Commission, an opinion on the impact of a media concentration on media pluralism and editorial independence, where the concentration is likely to affect the functioning of the internal market for media services.

Currently, the Commission has not requested the Media Board to draw up an opinion on this acquisition. The Commission continues to closely monitor the application of the EMFA in France and in all Member States and will follow up as appropriate. The EMFA is without prejudice to the application of EU competition law, including Regulation (EC) No 139/2004 on merger control, which applies in parallel.
